What happened across the app - launches, config imports, updates, team sign-in, sharing and more (separate from the connection log)
One hop through the bundled tvaVPN/WARP engine. Fastest.

Two hops: tvaVPN connects first, then Tor is built INSIDE that tunnel. The network you are on sees only tvaVPN’s obfuscated transport, never Tor — so this is the mode to use where Tor is blocked. Your exit is a Tor exit node.
Two hops: tvaVPN connects first, then Psiphon tunnels through it. Your exit IP becomes Psiphon\'s, so sites that block tvaVPN/WARP addresses open again.

Tor alone, without the tvaVPN tunnel. Your exit is a Tor exit node and your traffic passes three relays, which is the slowest and the most private of the modes. Tor has to reach the Tor network by itself here, so it uses bridges when it is blocked.

The reverse chain: Tor first, then the tvaVPN tunnel built INSIDE it. Your exit is a WARP address — the same as plain tvaVPN — but the network you are on sees only Tor, and cannot tell that a VPN tunnel exists at all. Use it where Cloudflare/WARP itself is blocked or throttled but Tor still gets through. Carries normal UDP, unlike the Tor-exit modes.

Three hops: Tor first, then Psiphon dialled through it. Your exit IP is Psiphon’s, reached from a Tor address, so sites that block Tor exit nodes open again while your own address stays behind Tor. The slowest mode.

The ping is a real delay test, like v2rayNG\'s: each config runs in the Xray core exactly as a direct connection would, and one request (generate_204) is sent through it. The number is the time for that request, handshake included. A config that carries nothing reports -1, with the reason: “Offline / server down” — the server\'s name does not resolve or its port is closed; “Filtered” — the network drops or resets the connection to the server (chaining it behind tvaVPN or Tor can help); “No response” — the server accepts connections but the config carried nothing (expired, wrong key or user, or its protocol is blocked); “Invalid config” — the Xray core refuses the config.

The engine started but Tor never reported any progress towards the Tor network. Check that the connection is up, then try the tvaVPN → Tor mode, which builds Tor inside the tunnel.

Tor chooses its own exit node, and a new one per circuit. No setting can pin it to a country.

The older gool (--gool-classic): WireGuard tunneled inside WireGuard. Use it if the modern mode does not connect on your network.
The engine’s default: a WireGuard WARP tunnel carried inside MASQUE, with its own identity registered from inside WARP, so you leave from a foreign location.

How Tor reaches the network when it is blocked.

Which country bridgedb hands out bridges for. Detection asks the network where you are, which is the request most likely to fail here.
How long Tor tries the direct path before falling back to bridges. Shorten it where Tor is definitely blocked.

Tor carries TCP only — in every app, on every platform. tvaVPN answers DNS over TCP inside Tor and drops other UDP, so QUIC-capable apps fall back to TCP. That is normal and nothing is leaking: dropped UDP goes nowhere, least of all around Tor. Expect noticeably higher latency, and expect the first connect to take a while — Tor downloads its directory before it can build a circuit.
